plugin_desc: Phoenix Contact FL SWITCH SNMP collection (IANA PEN 4346). Interface traffic is supplied by the shared Switch SNMP IF-MIB floor. Proven private device-health objects are redundant power-supply status (flWorkBasicPowerStat) and chassis temperature in degrees Celsius (flWorkFWCtrlActualDeviceTemperature). Optional firmware operational status (flWorkFWInfoOperStatus), firmware health text as a tag, and alarm-contact status (flWorkFWCtrlAlarmContactStatus) are collected when the device returns them. CPU and memory utilization are not collected because no private CPU or memory utilization scalar is published. Supported brands/models — Phoenix Contact FL SWITCH industrial Ethernet switches.
name: Switch

metrics.name: power_status
metrics.description: Redundant power-supply status of the Phoenix Contact FL SWITCH (flWorkBasicPowerStat). Native codes are unknown (1), supply 1 OK (3), supply 2 OK (4), and both supplies OK (5). A value other than 5 means a lost input or unknown power state.

metrics.name: device_temperature_celsius
metrics.description: Chassis temperature of the Phoenix Contact FL SWITCH in degrees Celsius (flWorkFWCtrlActualDeviceTemperature). Abnormally high temperatures may indicate blocked airflow or excessive ambient heat, and can trigger thermal protection or hardware damage if left unaddressed.

metrics.name: firmware_oper_status
metrics.description: Firmware operational state of the Phoenix Contact FL SWITCH (flWorkFWInfoOperStatus). Native codes are other (1), ok (2), and notOk (3). A value other than 2 indicates the firmware is not in normal running mode. The optional health-text string is collected as a tag, not a numeric metric.

metrics.name: alarm_contact_status
metrics.description: Alarm-contact status of the Phoenix Contact FL SWITCH (flWorkFWCtrlAlarmContactStatus). Native codes are open (1, alarm asserted) and closed (2, no alarm). An open contact means a configured alarm condition is active.

metrics.name: snmp_uptime
metrics.description: This metric indicates the uptime of the device since the last restart. By monitoring the uptime, network administrators can understand the stability and reliability of the device and identify potential reboot or failure issues.
